account: Researchers evaluated forecasts from Google Flood Hub and the Global Flood Awareness System (GloFAS) against river-flow observations and records of flood impacts in Mali. Four of the seven authors work for the Netherlands Red Cross data and digital team 510. The researchers are independent of Google, although one coauthor works at the Joint Research Centre, which contributes to GloFAS. The authors first presented the result in a European Geosciences Union abstract dated 14 March 2025. They posted a preprint on 7 January 2026, and the journal article appeared on 16 September 2026. Their results suggest that some early-action plans could extend from four to seven days without much loss of forecast skill. Performance varied across districts and thresholds, and no correctly predicted floods were found in the northern districts that were evaluated. At a seven-day lead time, Google Flood Hub’s false-alarm ratio was around 0.8 across discharge thresholds, compared with around 0.5 for GloFAS. The authors describe GloFAS as more balanced in several comparisons. They used a ten-day matching window to compare forecasts with reported impacts, which affects the interpretation of performance. This was a retrospective forecast evaluation, and it did not measure benefits from an implemented early action. No source reports that the Mali Red Cross protocol has adopted these forecasts or a seven-day lead time.

ai_role.statement: The authors compare Google Flood Hub's machine-learning forecasts with the physics-based GloFAS and with Mali's current trigger model on the same floods. They report that Flood Hub detects more floods than GloFAS at return-period thresholds but raises more false alarms. Any humanitarian benefit would depend on the Red Cross adopting the triggers and acting on them, which no source reports.

Four of the seven authors work for the Netherlands Red Cross data and digital team 510. The researchers are independent of Google, although one coauthor works at the Joint Research Centre, which contributes to GloFAS. The authors first presented the result in a European Geosciences Union abstract dated 14 March 2025. They posted a preprint on 7 January 2026, and the journal article appeared on 16 September 2026. Their results suggest that some early-action plans could extend from four to seven days without much loss of forecast skill. Performance varied across districts and thresholds, and no correctly predicted floods were found in the northern districts that were evaluated. At a seven-day lead time, Google Flood Hub’s false-alarm ratio was around 0.8 across discharge thresholds, compared with around 0.5 for GloFAS. The authors describe GloFAS as more balanced in several comparisons. They used a ten-day matching window to compare forecasts with reported impacts, which affects the interpretation of performance. This was a retrospective forecast evaluation, and it did not measure benefits from an implemented early action. No source reports that the Mali Red Cross protocol has adopted these forecasts or a seven-day lead time.

summary: A retrospective evaluation suggests that Google Flood Hub forecasts could extend some early-action plans in Mali from four to seven days, with frequent false alarms; no early action was measured.
taxonomy_note: A forecast-skill evaluation is read as task accuracy; no early action is documented.
title: Study suggests that Google Flood Hub and GloFAS forecasts could extend some flood early-action plans in Mali from four to seven days; Flood Hub produced frequent false alarms
unrated_because: The study measures forecast skill on past floods and reports no early action taken on these forecasts, so no group has a realized benefit to rate.
